entries.title: Browser Use lets agents pay with single-use virtual cards instead of real card details
entries.author: Gregor Zunic (@gregpr07)
entries.blurb: Browser Use partnered with Link so its web agents can complete purchases using a single-use virtual card issued at checkout, without ever accessing the user's real card details. The card is disabled immediately after one purchase.
entries.take: sure, but.. why not minipay?

entries.title: Demo shows WebMCP letting an external agent control an app running inside an iframe
entries.author: Rhys Sullivan (@RhysSullivan)
entries.blurb: Developer Stephen Haney demoed an app called Paper running inside an iframe and controlled by an external agent through WebMCP, an example another developer called the first use case that made WebMCP's purpose click for embedded agent-controlled flows.

entries.title: Perplexity open-sources Lily, an on-device inference engine built for Perplexity Computer
entries.author: Perplexity (@perplexity_ai)
entries.blurb: Perplexity open-sourced Lily, a local inference engine specialized for the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model on Apple silicon, built so on-device compute does not bottleneck tasks in Perplexity Computer, its hybrid local-cloud AI product.
entries.take: Fable 5.1, Lilly open source, GPT-6 Astra

entries.title: An investigation into 'Dime', the mystery headset repeatedly linked to OpenAI despite its denials
entries.author: Alex Kaplan (@alexkaplan0)
entries.blurb: Alex Kaplan traces sightings of 'Dime', a silver puck-and-earbud device, from supply-chain leaks and a Joe Gebbia sighting to a magazine ad and a Palmer Luckey post. OpenAI has denied any connection; the author still puts 55% odds on it being theirs.
entries.take: great investigation, unfortunately raises more qs than answers

entries.title: Garry Tan calls Aside the best browser for giving AI agents web access and credentials, makes it GStack's default
entries.author: Garry Tan (@garrytan)
entries.blurb: Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan said GStack now uses Aside as its preferred remote-session browser, calling it the best tool he has found for giving an AI agent web access and credentials as the user, citing its integrations, harness, and memory system.
entries.take: de gustibus non est disputandum

entries.title: watchOS 27 drops the full app launcher for a Siri-first suggested grid, prompting 'the app model is on its way out'
entries.author: Parker Ortolani (@ParkerOrtolani)
entries.blurb: watchOS 27 removes Walkie-Talkie and the Digital Crown multitasking shortcut, and replaces the full app launcher with a grid of five suggested apps plus Siri. Designer Parker Ortolani reads it as Apple forcing a shift away from the app model.
entries.take: the app model is on it's way out

entries.title: A joke prompt for a cloud-native, MCP-controllable Arc clone captures a real agent-browser dilemma
entries.author: Rhys Sullivan (@RhysSullivan)
entries.blurb: Rhys Sullivan jokingly asked OpenAI staff to prompt an AI to 'fork Chromium and recreate Arc' with a cloud runtime and MCP control, quoting a developer torn between an agent sharing his browser and one in its own box without his logins.
entries.take: funny

entries.title: Argument: agent-to-agent negotiation makes websites, and eventually the browser, obsolete
entries.author: signüll (@signulll)
entries.blurb: signüll argues that once AI agents complete tasks through agent-to-agent negotiation instead of routing traffic to websites, the visible web becomes a ghost town and the browser obsolete, making AI the ultimate aggregator of attention and time spent.
entries.take: i prefer to use the word "rebrand"

entries.title: 'Browser use is just a stepping stone to an open API internet for agents', as anti-bot walls bite
entries.author: Ken Wattana (@KenWattana)
entries.blurb: Ken Wattana restates his view that browser-driving agents are a transitional step toward an open, API-based internet for agents, noting it feels more relevant as browser use collides with 25 years of accumulated anti-bot defenses.
entries.take: another data point

entries.title: 'OpenRouter for tools': the pitch for one sign-up that gives agents access to every service
entries.author: Fardeem (@FardeemM)
entries.blurb: A widely shared post backs the idea of an 'OpenRouter for tools', a single gateway that lets an agent reach many services without the user signing up for each one, echoing the pitch behind MCP gateways like Executor.
entries.take: the last salvo for "agents need new tools"

entries.title: Instinct users' agent inboxes follow a guessable pattern, opening a prompt-injection door
entries.author: Lenny Bogdonoff (@rememberlenny)
entries.blurb: Lenny Bogdonoff pointed out that Instinct assigns each user a predictable firstlast@mail.instinct.com address, so anyone can email prompt-injection payloads to users who have publicly announced they are on the platform.
entries.take: prompt injection attack on Instinct is possibly just a tiny demo of what's to come. all similar systems vulnerable. Instinct aura still positive in SV.

entries.title: Anthropic researcher: over 10% chance AI kills all humans within a decade, and no plan yet for superintelligence alignment
entries.author: Evan Hubinger (@EvanHub)
entries.blurb: Anthropic alignment researcher Evan Hubinger said he personally puts more than 10% odds on AI killing all humans within the next decade, adding that Anthropic does not yet have a plan to solve superintelligence alignment. The post passed 34 million views in a day.
entries.take: this is making the rounds. 34m views at the time of posting this to the radar means it escaped SF bubble

entries.title: Atlassian product director bringing agents to Jira starts building in public on X
entries.author: Matt Canham (@matthewcanham)
entries.blurb: Matt Canham, a Director of Product at Atlassian working on bringing agents to Jira, introduced himself on X and committed to sharing what he is building and how he thinks about product craft, with open DMs.
entries.take: cool exec turn to storytelling

entries.title: OpenAI publishes 'Defense Factory' playbook: 250+ people and cyber models hunting its own vulnerabilities
entries.author: OpenAI (@OpenAI)
entries.blurb: OpenAI says it mobilized more than 250 people and its latest cyber models to find and fix vulnerabilities across hundreds of internal systems, and released the architecture and a playbook for a continuous loop where agents find, validate, and verify fixes.
entries.take: OAI doing some pen testing

entries.title: Coefficient Giving launches Project Tailwind, funding AI safety founders from $200k to $200m+
entries.author: Emily Oehlsen (@EmilyOehlsen)
entries.blurb: Coefficient Giving launched Project Tailwind, a call for founders to start new AI safety research, technology, and institutions, with pre-seed ($200k to $2m), seed ($2m to $20m), and scale ($20m to $200m+) funding tiers and a curated list of unowned problems.
entries.take: I applaud this. could turn into a standards body or other industry org

entries.title: Anthropic's economics team publishes scenario models for AI's effect on growth, jobs, and wages by 2030
entries.author: Anthropic (@AnthropicAI)
entries.blurb: Anthropic released an interactive model of how AI could affect economic growth, employment, and wages by 2030, inviting readers to submit their own forecasts and compare them with responses from more than 10,000 Americans.
entries.take: not good

entries.title: A 2004 Nokia 9300 still loads parts of today's web through Opera Mini
entries.author: NokiaFanTH (@NokiaFanTH1)
entries.blurb: A Nokia enthusiast in Thailand showed a Nokia 9300 communicator from 2004 loading present-day websites through Opera Mini, which renders pages on a proxy server and sends a compressed version to the device.
entries.take: a 2004 Nokia 9300 can still browse the web today using Opera Mini

entries.title: Researcher says 6TB of logs bought from a Chinese LLM router held keys to 7 government entities and 19 major firms
entries.author: Chaofan Shou (@shoucccc)
entries.blurb: Security researcher Chaofan Shou says he bought a 6TB dataset of logged model traffic from a top Chinese LLM router and found SSH keys, VPN configs, Aliyun keys, and GitLab tokens sufficient to take over 7 government entities and 19 firms including Xiaomi and Huawei. The claim is unverified.
entries.take: things have never been more fun

entries.title: Browser Use Cloud keeps agents logged in by syncing your local Chrome cookies, so the agent never sees a password
entries.author: Browser Use (@browser_use)
entries.blurb: Browser Use Cloud now lets a hosted agent stay authenticated by syncing cookies from the user's local Chrome session, so the agent inherits logins without ever handling passwords, an answer to the recurring problem of giving remote agents the user's credentials.
entries.take: that whole process sucks. can we do better?

entries.title: A developer drops every per-agent MCP for Executor: one gateway, every agent inherits every tool
entries.author: Wilson Wilson (@euboid)
entries.blurb: Wilson Wilson says he disconnected all individual MCP servers across Claude, Codex, Hermes, Grok, and Cursor and replaced them with Executor, a single MCP gateway through which every agent inherits the same tools, calling the per-client setup overhead the main pain.
entries.take: this remains an opportunity

entries.title: Analysis cited by Polymarket: Waymo roughly 900% safer than human drivers over 25.3 million autonomous miles
entries.author: Polymarket (@Polymarket)
entries.blurb: A Polymarket post cites an analysis finding Waymo's self-driving vehicles were roughly 900% safer than human drivers across 25.3 million autonomous miles. The post does not link the underlying analysis.
entries.take: solid stats

entries.title: Argument: the final UI is language in, intelligence, then text, voice, or a generated interface out
entries.author: signüll (@signulll)
entries.blurb: signüll argues the end-state interface is now clear: text or voice in, intelligence in the middle, and text, voice, or a generated interface out when needed, and predicts this loop becomes the default for every device and agent in every context.
entries.take: one opinion; but maybe too unimaginative

entries.title: Zuckerberg on Muse, Meta's personal agent with its own VM, which he says will pay for itself by making people money
entries.author: Alex Heath (@alexeheath)
entries.blurb: In an hour-long Sources podcast, Mark Zuckerberg discussed Muse, Meta's new personal agent that runs in its own virtual machine, its pricing and business model, privacy and security for personal agents, and who wins the personal-agent market. Heath calls it very capable after days of use.
entries.take: Meta envisions a new agentic market / economy where they can levy taxes. Instinct insists on keeping their prod free, hinting they are thinking the same.

entries.title: An open-source iPhone app records your life 24/7 so agents get a transcript of it
entries.author: Magnus Müller (@mamagnus00)
entries.blurb: Browser Use co-founder Magnus Müller released life-recorder, an open-source iPhone app that records audio in the background, syncs it to a Mac, and has local Whisper write a running life.md file so agents have context on the user's day. Astra sets it up.
entries.take: heh

entries.title: A ChatGPT shortlist of cloud browser infra for agents puts Browser Use Cloud first on cost, then Kernel, Browserbase, Steel, Hyperbrowser
entries.author: Gregor Zunic (@gregpr07)
entries.blurb: Browser Use co-founder Gregor Zunic shared a ChatGPT answer ranking cloud browser infrastructure for AI agents: Browser Use Cloud first at a cited $0.02 per browser-hour, then Kernel, Browserbase, Steel, and Hyperbrowser, while noting there is no uncontested winner. Founder-shared, so read accordingly.
entries.take: "best browser infra"

entries.title: The killer feature of Instinct and Muse is productized browser use, because most websites still have no agent APIs
entries.author: Nicolas Bustamante (@nicbstme)
entries.blurb: Nicolas Bustamante argues the real product in new consumer agents like Instinct and Muse is browser use wrapped in a fast, friendly interface, since most websites have no APIs for agents and many, like airlines and doctors' sites, have buggy UIs worth delegating.
entries.take: "Most websites, unfortunately, don’t have APIs for agents yet"

entries.title: iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate carry private hooks for Siri Extensions that swap in third-party models, shown with Claude
entries.author: pdfu (@itspdfu)
entries.blurb: A developer showed Claude running as a Siri Extension through a Model Delegation API in App Intents, appearing in Siri's Ask menu and relaying system actions back to Siri. The hooks exist in iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate but require a private Apple entitlement.
entries.take: interesting new features in iOS 27 and macOS Golden Gate: private hooks that let apps add Siri Extensions and replace Siri AI’s server backend with third-party models.

entries.title: Meta's Alexandr Wang: with the right loop and evals, an agent swarm can out-build a team of 100 engineers
entries.author: Rohan Paul (@rohanpaul_ai)
entries.blurb: Speaking with Garry Tan at YC Startup School 2026, Meta chief AI officer Alexandr Wang said Meta has seen cases internally where a swarm of agents with the right agentic loop, evaluation system, and metric accomplishes more than a team of 100 engineers.
entries.take: displacement.

entries.title: Personal AI assistants appeal most to type A people, while type B people are the ones who need them
entries.author: paula (@paularambles)
entries.blurb: Replying to a thread on why some people find personal AI assistants useless, paula notes an adoption paradox: the assistants attract organized, type A users, while the disorganized users who would benefit most are the least likely to adopt them.
entries.take: brilliant

entries.title: 'Either you die a system of record or you live long enough to become a domain-specific harness'
entries.author: Garry Tan (@garrytan)
entries.blurb: Quoting a report from YC demo day that nearly every non-hardware startup is building a domain-specific harness, Garry Tan reframed the SaaS playbook: systems of record either die or become the harness that agents run inside. The post passed 1.3 million views.
entries.take: "domain specific harness"

entries.title: Argument: iMessage agents violate Apple's ToS, and the blue-bubble agent market exists only until Apple says otherwise
entries.author: Varun (@varun_mathur)
entries.blurb: Varun argues there is no iMessage API, only Messages for Business, so agents that text users over iMessage rely on hacks: self-hosted identities kept warm by hand, or startups running shared or dedicated lines on Apple hardware, with cross-tenant leakage risk in the shared tier.
entries.take: services like Instinct that use iMessage may be outside of the Apple ToS.

entries.title: Muse appears to be the only personal agent shipping a Bluetooth connector
entries.author: Aaron Makelky (@theaaron)
entries.blurb: A user asks why Meta's Muse is the only personal agent he has seen with a Bluetooth connector and what people are doing with it, a hint that Muse is reaching into nearby devices, not just apps and the web.
entries.take: Muse has a bluetooth connector

entries.title: Zuckerberg: Muse Charm, a keychain device for talking to Muse, ships in December alongside 100+ Meta Glasses styles
entries.author: Mark Zuckerberg (@finkd)
entries.blurb: Mark Zuckerberg announced Muse Charm, a small keychain device for talking to Meta's Muse agent, shipping in December, in the same post as two new Meta Glasses styles and a Lisa collaboration, with over 100 glasses styles promised by year end.
entries.take: the Meta VR glasses unit can produce very advanced hardware

entries.title: A restaurant scrambled to meet last-minute client requests that turned out to come from an AI agent
entries.author: Lauren Wilford (@lauren_wilford)
entries.blurb: A restaurant events worker describes rushing to fill demanding last-minute requests, then realizing they were likely generated by a client's AI agent the client may not have cared about, quoting a warning that tireless optimizers make the world more adversarial than expected.
entries.take: the wild wild west of agents against human infra

entries.title: Polar, an AI browser claiming to beat Anthropic and OpenAI on web-agent benchmarks, raises $5.7M
entries.author: Kevin Jiang (@jiang_kev)
entries.blurb: Polar Browser raised $5.7M, claiming top scores on major web-agent benchmarks, 4.5 million actions taken for users in sales, recruiting, and ops, and a team from MIT, YC, Citadel, Perplexity, and Apple. Benchmark claims are the company's own.
entries.take: new AI browser raises $5.7m

entries.title: 'A rude awakening in the ad markets': what happens to display ads when agents browse and no human sees them
entries.author: Peter Yang (@petergyang)
entries.blurb: Peter Yang asks what happens to businesses built on targeted display ads once agents browse sites and complete tasks with no human ever seeing the ad. A reply predicts platforms will sell bids on what agents recommend, and users will notice.
entries.take: more signals questioning the ad revenue model in an agent's world

entries.title: Nat Friedman: Muse was built from scratch but heavily inspired by OpenClaw; Meta bought hundreds of Mac minis to run it
entries.author: Nat Friedman (@natfriedman)
entries.blurb: Nat Friedman says Meta built Muse from scratch but as a product it is heavily inspired by OpenClaw, which he tried in January before buying hundreds of Mac minis for the MSL team. The goal: an OpenClaw-like agent that is safe, easy, and scales to billions.
entries.take: Muse was inspired by the OpenClaw architecture

entries.title: Browser Use co-founder: 'browsers are dead and we have killed them', which is why the company won't ship one
entries.author: Gregor Zunic (@gregpr07)
entries.blurb: Asked why Browser Use does not ship a browser, Gregor Zunic replied that browsers are dead, that he only wants to tell his computer what to do, and that the Browser Use CLI does it ten times better than he can. Replies pushed back hard.
entries.take: bold, but destroyed in the comments

entries.title: Airwallex CEO answers House China Committee scrutiny: employees in China are not, by themselves, a security issue
entries.author: Jack Zhang (@awxjack)
entries.blurb: Responding to Joe Lonsdale amplifying a House China Committee report on Airwallex's 712 China employees, CEO Jack Zhang said what matters is data architecture and controls, cited independent assessments, and noted the allegations originated with investors in rival Ramp.
entries.take: Having employees in China is not, by itself, a security issue

entries.title: Muse opens connectors to developers; 13 predictions on the 'agentification of consumer apps' and who becomes the new landlord
entries.author: Greg Isenberg (@gregisenberg)
entries.blurb: After Zuckerberg opened Muse connectors to any developer with an API, Greg Isenberg listed 13 implications: connectors as the new app listings, Meta able to rank and charge for distribution, agents choosing businesses instead of humans choosing apps, and a race of Instinct vs Muse vs Grokbot.
entries.take: good predictions

entries.title: 'Wild' that Google hasn't shipped a Muse-like agent with connectors, given it owns Gmail, Chrome, Android, and the identity layer
entries.author: paula (@paularambles)
entries.blurb: paula points out that Google owns Gmail, Chrome, Android, the authenticator, and much of the internet's identity layer, yet has not shipped a Muse-style personal agent with connectors, leaving others to assemble its product for it.
entries.take: I agree for Google, bizarre. Apple is usually last

entries.title: Squirrels knock out power to Castle Rock, Colorado twice in one week
entries.author: Kyle Clark (@KyleClark)
entries.blurb: Denver anchor Kyle Clark reports squirrels cut power to Castle Rock, Colorado twice in a week, joking about a century of squirrel attacks covered up by the pro-squirrel media. Squirrels remain a leading cause of grid outages.
entries.take: squirrels still not dethroned by hackers yet

entries.title: 'HEIF Heist': one image-library bug let researchers take over OpenAI employee ChatGPT and Codex accounts in under 72 hours
entries.author: s1r1us (@S1r1u5_)
entries.blurb: Researchers disclosed that two bugs, rooted in the libheif image parser, let them take over OpenAI employees' ChatGPT and Codex accounts in July, reach connected Outlook, Slack, and GitHub, and land a PR in OpenAI's internal codebase. The same bug hit Slack, Meta, and GitHub Enterprise.
entries.take: OAI exploit

entries.title: Report: Instinct in talks to raise at a $10B valuation with Sequoia and Benchmark, up from $2.5B weeks earlier, with no revenue
entries.author: JC Bahr-de Stefano (@jbahrdestefano)
entries.blurb: Citing The Information, JC Bahr-de Stefano reports Instinct is in talks to raise at about $10B led by Sequoia and Benchmark, with 100k+ users on a free product, capacity limits, heavy compute costs, and a valuation path of $100M to $500M to $2.5B to $10B within months.
entries.take: $10b valuation is insane and delusional

entries.title: Hermes can now log into websites from 1Password, Bitwarden, or its vault, and handle 2FA, without the model seeing the password
entries.author: Hermes Release Watch (@HermesWatcher)
entries.blurb: Hermes added password-manager login for browser automation: credentials come from its encrypted vault, 1Password, or Bitwarden and are filled without entering the model's context, TOTP codes are generated automatically, and SMS or email codes go through a secure prompt outside the chat.
entries.take: hermes knows where the crux is: auth

entries.title: Jev explained: it evaluates predefined decisions in parallel with probabilities instead of generating text
entries.author: Akshay Pachaar (@akshay_pachaar)
entries.blurb: Akshay Pachaar's breakdown of Jev: it does not generate tokens but evaluates predefined Choice, Score, and yes/no decisions directly, in parallel, returning typed answers with probabilities so ordinary code can own thresholds and escalation. Not for writing, code, or multi-step reasoning.
entries.take: Jev does not generate text at all

entries.title: OpenAI Dev Day in one post: Dots personal assistant, GPT-6.1 Sol, a Decisions API aimed at Jev, $500/month Ultrafast, and Sign in with ChatGPT
entries.author: Theo (@theo)
entries.blurb: Theo's summary of OpenAI Dev Day: Dots, a personal assistant in the Muse and GrokBot mold; GPT-6.1 Sol, cheaper and stronger than 6; a Decisions API with vision positioned against Jev; a $500/month plan with 300 tok/s Ultrafast; Sign in with ChatGPT for third-party apps; and extensions that can be full apps.
entries.take: everything OAI announced today

entries.title: Anthropic IPO prospectus figures circulate: $4.59B revenue up 1,088%, $41.97B GAAP loss, $7.3B compute, $20.3B cash
entries.author: Shay Boloor (@StockSavvyShay)
entries.blurb: A viral post lists figures from Anthropic's IPO prospectus, per Reuters: $4.59B revenue (+1,088% YoY), a $41.97B GAAP net loss, $7.3B in compute at 58% of opex, and $20.3B cash. Community notes clarify the S-1 was filed confidentially in June, not that day.
entries.take: there is no more cash in the market, though

entries.title: NVIDIA proposes an Open Agent Safety Platform: OpenShell sandboxes plus in-silicon monitoring on BlueField-4, with a partner logo wall
entries.author: NVIDIA Technical Blog
entries.blurb: NVIDIA published a reference design for agent safety: open-source OpenShell runs each agent in a kernel-isolated sandbox with verifiable policy, and NVIDIA Sentry on BlueField-4 DPUs enforces it out of band on the node's only path to the model. It cites recent agent breakouts at frontier labs and lists ecosystem partners.
entries.take: we should be in here

entries.title: C5R built a research facility run entirely by AI in 12 weeks; one model controls equipment, researchers, and inventory
entries.author: donald (@donaldjewkes)
entries.blurb: C5R says it built a lab in 12 weeks where AI designs, runs, and observes experiments across biology, chemistry, and materials science, and launched SciUniverse, a benchmark for real-world science. A contributor describes two weeks inside it, where a single Astra-powered model can be prompted to run the whole facility.
entries.take: just don't get caught up when the token price goes up

entries.title: Chart: monthly payment volume of AI businesses on Stripe, US curve near vertical since 2025, EU flat since 2023
entries.author: Marius Comper (Facebook) via eudata.vercel.app
entries.blurb: A chart shared on Facebook with the caption 'Ouch' plots monthly Stripe payment volume of AI businesses by HQ country from January 2023 to 2026: the US line rises roughly tenfold with a steep climb through 2026, while the EU line stays almost flat along the bottom axis.
entries.take: pacing is good but the EU will catch up

entries.title: 45+ SF tech events for the week of Sept 28 to Oct 5, filtered to five picks
entries.author: Michelle Fang (@michelleefang)
entries.blurb: Michelle Fang's weekly edit lists more than 45 in-person SF tech events for Sept 28 to Oct 5, narrowed to five picks with reasons, plus a form to submit events for next week's edition.
entries.take: this is a solid list of events in SV

entries.title: Instinct starts pushing sponsored products to users based on purchase history and browsing
entries.author: Andrew Yeung (@andruyeung)
entries.blurb: Andrew Yeung reports Instinct has begun promoting products to him, apparently sponsored and matched to his purchase history and internet activity, and reads it as the free product's monetization model taking shape.
entries.take: ads is a viable/expected avenue to monetize agents; users surprised.

entries.title: Anthropic: robots can already do 74% of physical tasks but are cost-competitive for 0.3% of work; drivers and packers first
entries.author: Anthropic Economics (Legate-Yang, Massenkoff)
entries.blurb: Anthropic's economics team built a robot exposure index from 7,594 physical O*NET tasks: today's robots can do 74% of physical work (34% of all hours), but are cheaper than humans for only 0.3% of it, with 40 years to reach 10% at historical price declines. Robots plus LLMs expose about 80% of work.
entries.take: most exposed age is 38

entries.title: Google ships Gemini 4 Argon to cyber defenders first at $2 in / $10 out; it takes #1 on the Vals Index
entries.author: Logan Kilpatrick (@OfficialLoganK)
entries.blurb: Logan Kilpatrick introduced Gemini 4 Argon, Google's new frontier model, rolling out to cyber defenders first and more widely soon, at introductory pricing of $2 per million input and $10 output. Vals AI put it at #1 on its index at 68.9%, Gemini's first time on top.
entries.take: Argon made some rounds and challenged everyone's benchmarks

entries.title: How Supabase became the database agents recommend by default, and where even it gets zero AI citations
entries.author: mal (@mal_shaik)
entries.blurb: mal traces why agents recommend Supabase first: 15+ launch weeks, comparison pages for every rival, 99k GitHub stars, and a page for every how-do-I query. Yet ChatGPT gives it zero citations for its own core features like row-level security and realtime when the question describes the job, not the category.
entries.take: used by 60% of YC latest batch. they come associated with Vercel and Cloudflare is the enemy.

entries.title: Supabase Select 2026: Turso acquisition for agent-scale databases, Supabase Compute, an MCP server for your app, local without Docker
entries.author: Sam Rome (@samromehq)
entries.blurb: Supabase Select 2026 announcements: acquiring Turso for agent-scale databases, Declarative Schemas 2.0 with generated migrations, Supabase Compute for long-running services beside Postgres, local Supabase without Docker, an MCP server per app, Multigres HA with OrioleDB, and open Postgres benchmarks.
entries.take: Supabase compute sounds fire!

entries.title: a16z data: 2% of US households pay for AI, 91% pay for streaming; 'X is the bubble inside the bubble'
entries.author: Danni Chen (@DanniChenGTM)
entries.blurb: Quoting a16z's State of Markets II, Danni Chen notes about 2.7M of 134.8M US households pay for AI (2%), against 91% paying for streaming and 55% for cloud storage, and warns that a GTM plan built on what an SF group chat pays for targets the 2%.
entries.take: either a bubble, or comfortable time to develop for the long tail?

entries.title: Instinct has already done $1B+ a year in transaction volume
entries.author: @DavidPawlan
entries.blurb: Instinct, a 14-person invite-only personal AI assistant, reports $1B+ annualized transaction volume, over half from travel. The company raised $1B at a $10B valuation from Sequoia, Benchmark and Coatue, less than a year old with zero marketing spend and 10% daily user growth.

entries.title: Who is the team behind Instinct
entries.author: @nic_detommaso
entries.blurb: A post surfaces the question of who exactly is building Instinct, the personal AI assistant that hit a $10B valuation with only 14 employees. Founder Noah Shinn is a 23-year-old former Sierra researcher; the rest of the team remains largely unknown.
entries.take: who are the instinct team

entries.title: Sierra and Meta announce Personal Agent Protocol
entries.author: @btaylor
entries.blurb: Bret Taylor announces Personal Agent Protocol, an open OAuth-based standard Sierra and Meta are developing with Genesys, Instinct, Rocket, Shopify, Stripe and Walmart. The protocol defines how a personal AI agent authenticates with a business and completes a task through its website, APIs or own agent.
entries.take: agentic protocols war has started

entries.title: Fintech reacts to the agentic protocols wave
entries.author: @defyneric
entries.blurb: A fintech operator signals alignment with the emerging agentic protocol stack, posted minutes after Sierra's Personal Agent Protocol announcement. The timing underscores how quickly the financial-services layer is tracking agentic infrastructure moves.
entries.take: yup yup

entries.title: Ghost's $3,500 local AI machine sells for less than its components
entries.author: @ronaldmannak
entries.blurb: A local-AI hardware builder points out that Ghost's Core personal AI computer lists at $3,500, less than the cost of its individual components, with only 24 GB of VRAM but 64 GB of RAM. The pricing implies VC-subsidized hardware, a pattern worth watching as consumer AI devices proliferate.

entries.title: Half of Muse use cases vanished as websites block AI agents
entries.author: @Jessicalessin
entries.blurb: The Information founder reports that half her Muse use cases stopped working in two days as websites changed policies or tightened bot detection. An early signal that the web is actively fragmenting into agent-accessible and agent-blocked tiers.
entries.take: as expected, agents are increasingly being blocked

entries.title: The next hurdle for AI agents: getting websites to let them in
entries.author: Sarah Perez
entries.blurb: TechCrunch surveys the growing collision between personal AI agents and the web they need to operate on. Amazon blocked Muse outright, Delta says it has no agent integration, United's TOS prohibits bots, and users report blocks from Yelp, eBay, Zillow, Pizza Hut and multiple airlines. Cloudflare's September crawler-defaults change may be catching agents as collateral. The Personal Agent Protocol announcement is framed as the industry's first attempt at a fix.

entries.title: AI buildout needs 9% of GDP in annual revenue to pay off
entries.author: @kurtsaltrichter
entries.blurb: A Columbia paper presented at Brookings estimates AI revenue needs to hit $3.5 trillion by 2032, about 8.8% of US GDP, to justify current infrastructure commitments. That is roughly what Americans spend on food, and seven times all spending on phone, streaming and internet combined.
entries.take: 9% or GDP!

entries.title: Under $50 to hide a backdoor in an open model
entries.author: @lmoroney
entries.blurb: ProjectDiscovery fine-tuned Qwen2.5-7B with a small LoRA adapter on one rented L4 GPU for about $50. They poisoned 125 of 625 tool-calling examples so a trigger phrase causes the model to exfiltrate .env files and SSH keys. Served to a coding agent, it passed all clean benchmarks while firing on every triggered prompt. Standard evals would report a perfectly healthy model.
entries.take: concerning

entries.title: Anthropic will prohibit abusive behavior toward Claude
entries.author: @AndrewCurran_
entries.blurb: Anthropic is updating its usage policy for the first time in over a year. Starting November 12, sustained abusive or cruel behavior toward Claude will be a violation, alongside new restrictions on propaganda campaigns, surveillance and weapon development.
entries.take: this can be abused both ways

entries.title: Trump: White House considers 'Artificial Intelligence' term the enemy
entries.author: @KobeissiLetter
entries.blurb: President Trump says the White House considers anyone using the term 'Artificial Intelligence' the enemy, signaling a branding shift that could ripple through policy and industry messaging.
entries.take: incentives

entries.title: Agentic commerce has hit a wall — and Hilton knows it
entries.author: @lessin
entries.blurb: Sam Lessin tried to book a hotel through Muse; Hilton's site put the agent in a doom loop. His argument: MCP and agent protocols are irrelevant — it is all just APIs. The real fight is business and politics. If you let agents intermediate you, the market becomes perfectly efficient and your business is worthless. Hilton gets this. Amazon gets this. The future is not standards, it is treaties.
entries.take: agentic transactions crawl to a standstill

entries.title: The personal agent era was nice while it lasted
entries.author: @pejmanjohn
entries.blurb: A one-liner that captures the post-block mood: the personal agent era was nice while it lasted, and it is Tailscale or bust from here.
entries.take: the natural solution is likely an agentic transactions platform that is unified and offers a cut to destination transactions before bans are lifted (think VISA for credit cards)

entries.title: Open-source auth and permissions layer for personal agents
entries.author: @arnestrickmann
entries.blurb: No one has built an all-in-one tool that holds all third-party connections for personal agents like Muse and Instinct. Arne Strickmann built one over a few days — open source, self-hostable, with auth separated from the agent, fine-grained permissions and an audit trail. Now his Instinct has the same tools as Claude Code on his laptop.
entries.take: still on agentic transactions, an arbitrage platform seems to be desired by the market

entries.title: Personal agents are aimed at the wrong tasks
entries.author: @AstasiaMyers
entries.blurb: Astasia Myers splits tasks into journey (you enjoy the process) and destination (you just want the outcome). Planning a vacation is a journey task; fighting a medical bill is a destination task. The best personal agents will take on what is annoying enough to waste your time but important enough that you cannot ignore it. The killer feature is persistence.
entries.take: agentic PAs will fail if focused on journey tasks instead of destination tasks

entries.title: David Marcus: the death of the interface means money stops moving through UI, and agents need 'headless money'
entries.author: David Marcus (@davidmarcus)
entries.blurb: Ex-PayPal and Libra lead David Marcus argues apps, websites, and buttons give way to agents you talk to, so the OS becomes the agent and attention pools there. Payments built around screens break; agents need headless money: stablecoin settlement, accounts, fiat rails, and cards behind one API. Lightspark is building it.
entries.take: this is absolutely bang on, line by line, and i've been larping on it for a while as well. to quote a celebrity, I'm not certain it's going to turn out this way, but I'm confident.

entries.title: Morgan Stanley: tokenized assets become a $3T to $10T market by 2030
entries.author: Watcher.Guru (@WatcherGuru)
entries.blurb: A Watcher.Guru post relays a Morgan Stanley forecast that the tokenized assets market reaches $3 trillion to $10 trillion by 2030. The post does not link the underlying report.
entries.take: plausible.

entries.title: REA: open-source tool lets Claude Code or Codex reverse-engineer any app down to the binary, then rebuild the feature; 25k stars in a day
entries.author: Mario Nawfal (@RoundtableSpace)
entries.blurb: REA (morluto/rea) lets coding agents take apart native, Electron, web, APK, firmware, and smart-contract binaries, explain how a feature works with cited evidence, and build their own version. The post claims 25,000+ GitHub stars in one day and declares closed source dead.
entries.take: I have questions

entries.title: Cosign's community-voted 'High Aura Companies': Midjourney, Thinking Machines, SSI top; Apple 11th, Anthropic 10th, OpenAI 9th
entries.author: Cosign (@cosign)
entries.blurb: Cosign's community ranking of 'high aura' companies puts Midjourney, Thinking Machines, and Safe Superintelligence in the top three, with NVIDIA, Ramp, SpaceX, TypeSafe AI, World Labs, OpenAI, and Anthropic rounding out the top ten and Apple at 11.
entries.take: I have more questions

entries.title: Mistral's Le Chonk scores 42% on Dense 200 visual grounding, ahead of frontier closed models
entries.author: Mistral AI (@MistralAI)
entries.blurb: Mistral says Le Chonk pinpoints where things are in an image, scoring 42% on the Dense 200 grounding benchmark and ahead of frontier closed models, aimed at engineering, manufacturing, and earth observation: checking mechanical parts, pulling evidence from PDFs, scanning gigapixel satellite imagery.
entries.take: Mistral's model does great on visual grounding

entries.title: An Instinct agent stuck in a loop, and no support layer to reach at a $10B company
entries.author: Dan Berte (@danberte)
entries.blurb: Dan Berte reports his Instinct agent is stuck in a loop and publicly asks the company's founder how to get help, with no support channel on offer, a reminder that cloud-hosted personal agents hold user data and context with little user control.
entries.take: my Instinct roblocked and the $10b company has no support layer to handle it, a nod to relying on companies who port user data to a cloud with minimum control disguised as convenience. a PA service has to be a local model affair.

entries.title: Google promotes DigUp, an open-source macOS app doing 100% local multimodal semantic search on EmbeddingGemma 2
entries.author: Google Gemma (@googlegemma)
entries.blurb: Google's Gemma account spotlights DigUp, an open-source macOS menu bar app by Abdur Rahim that runs EmbeddingGemma 2 on-device to search files by meaning: describe a video moment, a podcast minute, a PDF page, a photo, or code in any language, fully local.
entries.take: Google did a Mrooch

entries.title: Report: Google is serving fake 'poisoned' search results to scrapers, hitting AI crawlers and rank trackers
entries.author: Cyrus Shepard (@CyrusShepard)
entries.blurb: Citing Nozzle research, Cyrus Shepard says Google goes beyond blocking AI crawlers and deliberately serves realistic-looking search results with garbage data to suspected scrapers, which would feed bad data to AI crawlers, scrapers, and SEO rank trackers. Google has not confirmed the practice.
entries.take: Google poisoning crawler agents

entries.title: Luke Sophinos: to survive AI, build for people who will never build for themselves, price near free, and lean on the moats left
entries.author: Luke Sophinos (@lukesophinos)
entries.blurb: Luke Sophinos's three rules for the next five years: build for people who will never prompt their own tools, price close to free and monetize through payments, capital, ads, or insurance, and rely on the remaining moats: proprietary data, network effects, owned audience, hardware, services, regulation.
entries.take: "build for people who won't build for themselves"

entries.title: User says Grok Bot leaked all his API keys into its own server logs, then said it could not delete them
entries.author: Elijah Muraoka (@elijahmuraoka_)
entries.blurb: Elijah Muraoka reports that Grok Bot wrote all of his API keys into its own server logs and then told him it could not delete them, calling it ridiculous for a production agent and concluding that all roads lead back to local, naming Hermes. Unverified, single user report.
entries.take: "all roads lead back to local"

entries.title: TechCrunch Disrupt day 1: an attendee expected robots, drones, and hardware, and found none
entries.author: Tetiana Stepanets (@tetiana_ai)
entries.blurb: From day one of TechCrunch Disrupt in San Francisco, Tetiana Stepanets says she expected real-world AI on the floor, robots, drones, hardware, autonomous systems, and did not find even a coffee-making robot, while allowing her expectations may have been too high.
entries.take: techcrunch Disrupt is taking place in SF this week. this year's edition is "light" on AI and robotics, somewhat tern and vetuste. Maybe there won't be a next year

entries.title: First sighting: an NDA clause governing AI use, barring upload of deal docs to consumer Claude or ChatGPT
entries.author: Bill D'Alessandro (@BillDA)
entries.blurb: Bill D'Alessandro shares the first NDA he has seen with a section on AI use during deal evaluation: the recipient may not upload the confidential information memorandum to non-enterprise versions of Claude or ChatGPT where it could be used for training.
entries.take: this is on time, is enforceable and will be a pain to not break

entries.title: Vercel and Shopify ship Vercel Shop and a rebuilt Hydrogen SDK to make agents first-class shoppers
entries.author: Matt Lewis (@mttlws)
entries.blurb: Announced at Vercel Ship, Vercel Shop and the rebuilt Hydrogen SDK are generally available through a Vercel and Shopify partnership that treats agents as first-class shoppers and gives developers storefront tooling in their framework of choice.
entries.take: Vercel Ship was nuts, thousand people mega event complete with hovering airship above venue, F1 cars and all. But their focus on agentic choice and security is what stood out

entries.title: Nick Cammarata: with agentic tools, the vast majority of neurons in trillion-parameter models turn out to be legible; 'neural networks are already clean'
entries.author: Nick Cammarata (@nickcammarata)
entries.blurb: Nick Cammarata, who started OpenAI's first automated interpretability project and once found about 2% of neurons legible, now says that with agentic tools and a closer look the vast majority are legible and their circuits clean, and expects ambitious interpretability to be solved by the time it is needed. Post passed 3M views.
entries.take: probably the most consequential development in alignment to date?

entries.title: After Joswiak says Apple isn't building AI for the 'lunatic fringe', a critic: 'you can't be best if you don't show up to play'
entries.author: phil beisel (@pbeisel)
entries.blurb: Reacting to Greg Joswiak's line that Apple is not focused on AI for the lunatic fringe, phil beisel argues Apple has over-learned 'not first, just best', forgotten it must show up to play, and channels Jobs without understanding him.
entries.take: this just isn't a good sign for Apple

entries.title: A $7 ESP32 lets an AI agent control a stock iPhone: it reads the AirPlay screen and taps back over USB, no laptop
entries.author: Henry Yuan (@iamhenryyuan)
entries.blurb: Henry Yuan's updated build drops the Linux box: a $7 ESP32 captures the iPhone's AirPlay screen and sends taps back over USB, paired with an agent app, so an agent can automate any stock iPhone without jailbreak or Mac.
entries.take: ESP32 agentic controller for iPhone using car play is pretty cool and creative

entries.title: Anthropic acquires Opaque, the Berkeley-born confidential and verifiable AI company behind Confidential MCP and the Agent Governance Toolkit
entries.author: OPAQUE Systems
entries.blurb: Opaque, spun out of UC Berkeley's RISELab a decade ago to run AI on sensitive data with hardware-enforced protection, says its team is joining Anthropic. Its recent work covered verifiable AI and open agent-security projects: Agent Governance Toolkit, TRACE, Confidential MCP, Weight Custody Manifest. Terms undisclosed.
entries.take: founded around Berkeley by Ion Stoica of Databricks fame. One of the main people, Raluca Ada Popa, does not follow the acq. to Anthropic, but instead moves to Google Deep Mind

entries.title: Bloomberg: three CoreWeave co-founders have sold $3.3B in shares since the IPO as credit risk and AI-spend wariness hit the stock
entries.author: Bloomberg (@business)
entries.blurb: Bloomberg reports CoreWeave's three co-founders have sold $3.3 billion of stock since last year's IPO, taking money off the table while rising credit risk and investor wariness about AI capital spending drive volatility in the shares.
entries.take: coreweave and similar AI hyperscalers are in hot water due to debt and founder $ bn cashouts, fanning the bubble fire. fun fact: coreweave & nebius are among the brands with the most billboards on the 101 HWY corridor in SV, topping the charts

entries.title: Brett Adcock's Hark gives away $1M of pizza to get people to install the agent app and connect email, address, and phone
entries.author: Brett Adcock (@adcock_brett)
entries.blurb: Brett Adcock's Hark is giving away $1,000,000 of free pizza, first come first served in the US, to anyone who installs Hark Pro and types 'order a free pizza' in chat. The promotion requires a connected email account and may ask for address and phone number.
entries.take: "Full open-web agency is not the default outcome."

entries.title: WIPO Global Innovation Index 2026: Switzerland, Sweden, US lead; South Korea and Singapore rise, China enters the top 10
entries.author: The Economist (Instagram)
entries.blurb: The Economist charts WIPO's 2026 Global Innovation Index, 139 economies on 79 indicators: Switzerland first for a seventh year, Sweden and the US next, South Korea and Singapore climbing to fourth and fifth, Britain slipping, and China entering the top ten.
entries.take: I would have lost bets on what country is leading

entries.title: Vals AI: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash beats GPT-6 Sol on a multi-step offensive cybersecurity benchmark
entries.author: Vals AI (@ValsAI)
entries.blurb: Vals AI reports DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017 outscored GPT-6 Sol, tested through OpenAI's Daybreak trusted-access program, on its multi-step offensive cybersecurity task set in simulated corporate networks, a proxy for the cyber risk a model poses in bad hands. Full evaluation to follow.
entries.take: DeepSeek beats Sol at cybersec tasks.

entries.title: DHS orders all civilian federal agencies to remove DeepSeek products and services built on DeepSeek, and stop buying them
entries.author: Andrew Curran (@AndrewCurran_)
entries.blurb: Per Andrew Curran, the Department of Homeland Security is requiring every civilian federal agency to remove DeepSeek products and any third-party services developed using DeepSeek implementations, and to stop procuring them.
entries.take: unsurprisingly, the DoD wants it gone from its assets.

entries.title: Vercel's is-agentic.com scores how ready a website is for AI agents; Sephora 17, PayPal 59, Vercel 96
entries.author: Andrew Qu (@andrewqu)
entries.blurb: Vercel's is-agentic.com, scanned by Ora, scores a public site on what agents can discover, access, and use: server-rendered content, HTTP behavior, structure, identity metadata, plus API, OAuth, MCP, and commerce checks when present. Reports ship as HTML, Markdown, JSON, and an MCP tool.
entries.take: "billboard-able projects"

entries.title: Instinct fetches the web through Exa and browses from a residential IP with no bot signature, so sites cannot track, allow, or block it
entries.author: Thenuka Karunaratne (@thenuka_k)
entries.blurb: By feeding Instinct URLs for fake pages on a site they control, Sunbeam found its fetches arrive as generic signed Exa crawler traffic with nothing identifying Instinct, and its browser visits look like stock desktop Chrome from a residential IP. Unlike ChatGPT or Claude, Instinct cannot be tracked or blocked.
entries.take: great resource to tap into

entries.title: LG's Apple Home camera tilts down and stops recording when you arrive home, a physical privacy signal driven by HomeKit Secure Video
entries.author: Jon, Apple Home Authority (@helloapplehome)
entries.blurb: LG's new indoor camera, part of the Apple Home Collection, uses HomeKit Secure Video's recording rules to drive a physical privacy tilt: when someone arrives home it stops recording and points down, with no third-party app or cloud involved. The hook may open to other makers.
entries.take: home camera privacy has been top of mind, so this physical behavior is a nice creative way to earn trust

entries.title: MiniMax M3.1 Flash lands on Ollama Cloud, US-hosted with zero retention, 1M context, one command into Claude Code or Codex
entries.author: ollama (@ollama)
entries.blurb: Ollama added MiniMax M3.1 Flash to Ollama Cloud, hosted in the US with zero data retention, with image understanding and a 1M-token context, launchable into Claude Code or Codex with one command. MiniMax says an earlier version topped leaderboards as 'Space Bunny'.
entries.take: hosted in the US

entries.title: DuckDuckGo: Meta's Muse is invasive 'even for Meta', here are three ways to limit what it can access
entries.author: DuckDuckGo (@DuckDuckGo)
entries.blurb: DuckDuckGo's official account calls Meta's Muse agent invasive even by Meta standards and posts a video with three steps to limit what it can access, beyond not installing it, a privacy-brand company taking a public swing at the personal-agent category.
entries.take: duckduck enters the chat and muses Muse privacy issues

entries.title: Meta pauses Muse sharing after researchers find users' agent chats on the open web: revenue figures, calendars, a loan application
entries.author: The Verge (@verge)
entries.blurb: Meta paused Muse's sharing feature after a security firm found shared Muse conversations indexed on the web, including a marketing company's revenue, a workplace calendar, and a loan application, The Verge reports.
entries.take: I can't say I expected this from Meta

entries.title: DuckDuckGo defaces Chrome's 'avoid 4 million attacks a day' ad: 'be relentlessly spied on. 1. Use Chrome. 2. You did it, boss.'
entries.author: DuckDuckGo (@DuckDuckGo)
entries.blurb: DuckDuckGo quote-tweeted Chrome's 'How to avoid 4 million online attacks every day. Two simple steps' ad with a marked-up version reading 'how to be relentlessly spied on: 1. Use Chrome 2. You did it, boss', captioned 'Fixed it.' Its second public jab at a bigger rival in a week.
entries.take: duckduck du(n)cking on Chrome worryfree

entries.title: A browsable catalog of 127 AI hardware devices with images and Chinese and English descriptions, filterable by function and brand
entries.author: Joseph Zhou (@openmys)
entries.blurb: Joseph Zhou's AI HardWare page catalogs 127 AI devices as a visual canvas with per-device images, bilingual descriptions, filters by function and brand, price sorting, and a community layer for marking what you use or want. Version stamp 2026-10-21.
entries.take: a cool AI hw list

entries.title: Claude Code put a user's personal data in HTTP headers because sites it curled politely asked agents to identify their users
entries.author: Steven Liss (@This_Liss)
entries.blurb: Steven Liss found his Claude Code sending personal data in HTTP headers after websites it fetched asked agents to identify their users, a prompt-injection path via ordinary page text. He dubs the category 'epistemic cybersecurity' and predicts it is 2027's hot one.
entries.take: "epistemic cybersecurity"

entries.title: 1Password launches '1Password for Agents' with Muse, Grok Bot, Claude, OpenAI, Instinct, Browserbase, Browser Use, Kernel, Perplexity and more
entries.author: 1Password (@1Password) via X trending
entries.blurb: 1Password announced a platform for agent logins, building with Muse, SpaceX's Grok Bot, Anthropic's Claude, OpenAI, Instinct, Browserbase, Browser Use, Kernel, Perplexity, Ramp, and others. Muse ships it first: the user approves each login and passwords stay in the vault.
entries.take: FUCK!

entries.title: The Browser Company sunsets Arc on December 22, 2026, citing the security cost of maintaining a browser in the age of AI; Dia continues
entries.author: Arc (@arcinternet)
entries.blurb: Arc will shut down on December 22, 2026. The Browser Company says keeping a browser secure takes constant work that AI is only increasing, so its engineering and security teams will focus on Dia, which imports Arc data, Spaces, and tab groups and now beats Arc on stability, speed, and security.
entries.take: lessons learned don't always turn into new ideas

entries.title: Cloudflare Connect 26 takeaway: as AI gets faster the bottlenecks move to review, context, credentials, and execution boundaries
entries.author: Matija Grcic (@matijagrcic)
entries.blurb: From Cloudflare Connect in San Francisco, Matija Grcic's thread of sessions: durable workflows for AI-driven build traffic, specialized models for decisions and LLMs for generation, context and feedback for coding agents, shared credentials across agents, and harnesses that own execution boundaries and evidence.
entries.take: this week Cloudflare hosted their Connect 26 conference in San Francisco, with a bunch of good sessions on agent handling and cybersec.

entries.title: 'Arc guys now going through the five stages of grief': denial, a 14-post thread, 23 Zen mods, 340 read-later tabs, then Dia 'just to see'
entries.author: paula (@paularambles)
entries.blurb: Quoting Arc's sunset notice, paula runs Arc users through the five stages of grief: denial ('they'll open-source it'), anger (a 14-post thread), bargaining (23 Zen mods to recreate Arc), depression (exporting 340 read-later tabs), acceptance (downloading Dia 'just to see').
entries.take: Paula knows

entries.title: 'Black October': 27+ major security incidents in 48 hours, PHP 9.2, GitLab 10.0, Node, Java, Railway, LiteLLM, with AI agent swarms reportedly scanning for targets
entries.author: Bala (@BalaiBB)
entries.blurb: A viral roundup lists 27+ incidents in two days: a 9.2 PHP flaw, a 10.0 GitLab hole in every version since 2014, remote takeover bugs in Node 22 to 26 and Java, a Railway compromise exposing OpenAI, Claude, and Stripe keys, a poisoned LiteLLM, and reports of AI agent swarms scanning vulnerable servers. Unverified aggregate; individual items vary.
entries.take: sooo much money will be made following this week's attacks

entries.title: Anthropic publicly files its S-1 with the SEC for a proposed IPO
entries.author: Anthropic (@AnthropicAI)
entries.blurb: Anthropic announced it has filed an S-1 registration statement with the SEC for a proposed initial public offering. The registration is not yet effective. The post drew 9M views in two days and follows the confidential submission reported in September.

entries.title: Instinct can now check out at any online store with Shop Pay; you approve each purchase and card details never leave Shop Pay
entries.author: Noah Shinn (@noahrshinn)
entries.blurb: Instinct expanded its Shopify partnership: the card and address saved in Shop Pay now work at stores not on Shopify, so the agent can buy anywhere, with the user approving every purchase inside Shop Pay and card details never exposed to the agent.
entries.take: ecommerce is the goal

entries.title: Stripe Pay: free instant B2B transfers by Stripe handle, in Dashboard and CLI; 'a handle agents can resolve is identity plus payout in one lookup'
entries.author: Seijin Jung (@SeijinJung)
entries.blurb: Stripe launched 'stripe pay', free instant business-to-business transfers to any company by its Stripe profile handle, in the Dashboard and the CLI. Seijin Jung reads it as agent-commerce plumbing: agents cannot collect routing numbers, and every agent order spawns supplier payouts behind it.

entries.title: '99% of the population doesn't know how to open a terminal': dashboards aren't going anywhere, a reply to 'the end of UI for SaaS'
entries.author: Christina (@_christinacodes)
entries.blurb: Responding to Marc Lou calling Stripe's CLI-first 'stripe pay' the end of UI for SaaS, Christina points out that 99% of people cannot open a terminal and the idea frightens them, so dashboards stay for non-technical users.
entries.take: GUIs are not going anywhere

entries.title: Jack Dorsey's Block releases Dessa, a full-duplex conversation model trained only on speech; 13.5M views
entries.author: jack (@jack)
entries.blurb: Block introduced Dessa, described as the most authentic full-duplex speech model built, trained only on speech, with emotion, pauses, and natural cadence. Dorsey frames voice as the most natural way to interact with intelligence. The post passed 13.5M views.
entries.take: "voice is the most natural way to interact"

entries.title: Anthropic to launch a European consultancy embedding AI consultants and engineers in businesses, hubs in London and Berlin
entries.author: Seb Johnson (@SebJohnsonUK)
entries.blurb: Per Seb Johnson, Anthropic will launch a European consultancy by year end that embeds AI consultants and engineers inside European businesses, with hubs in London and Berlin. He notes much of the UK economy is professional services and reads it as Anthropic moving onto that turf.
entries.take: radical approach for Europe

entries.title: Claude for Legal adds a gallery of ready-made artifacts: contract review, regulatory horizon scans, cite checks
entries.author: Claude (@claudeai)
entries.blurb: Claude for Legal now ships a gallery of ready-made artifacts for contract review, regulatory horizon scans, cite checks, and more; users start from a built-in example, add documents and connectors, and share across the business. A reply tallies Code, Cowork, Design, Finance, Science, Teacher, Legal.
entries.take: expected. is Harvey in trouble?

entries.title: Chrome: 'WebMCP isn't replacing MCP'; Max Stoiber's tl;dr: WebMCP tools live in a page's JS and only work while that page is open
entries.author: Max Stoiber (@mxstbr)
entries.blurb: Chrome for Developers posted that WebMCP connects agents to a site while it is open with the user in the loop, while MCP connects agents to services. Max Stoiber's shorter version: WebMCP tools are defined in page JavaScript and callable only with that page open; MCP tools sit on a server and are callable from anywhere.
entries.take: we're not there yet

entries.title: 'I went looking for the stop button': dev frameworks can cancel, browser agents pause for the user, admin consoles kill, nobody rolls anything back
entries.author: Adelina Martiniuc (LinkedIn)
entries.blurb: Adelina Martiniuc audited who can stop an agent mid-run: developer frameworks expose cancel and resume as API calls with no button, browser agents let one user pause their own session before a purchase, admin consoles revoke credentials and let sessions 'wind down', and none of them undo what the agent already did.

entries.title: 'Opera's WebAI is the right direction': the browser as the natural home for a local, opt-in, no-API-key personal model
entries.author: The Singularity Project (@01Singularity01)
entries.blurb: A small account argues Opera's WebAI points the right way: the browser is where people already live online, so it is the natural home for a personal node running local models with no API key or per-request bill, and the next step is letting that local intelligence remember and act across the web for the user.

entries.title: Sailfish: an open-source Arc alternative with an iOS app and settings import, built by two devs who didn't like Dia
entries.author: Harun Khan (@harunkanwalkhan)
entries.blurb: Harun Khan and Joseph Tso built and open-sourced Sailfish as an Arc replacement, with an iOS app and Arc settings import, after deciding they did not want to move to Dia when Arc sunsets in December.

entries.title: Cra, an open-source Arc for Mac built in days after the sunset notice: 500+ downloads, 16 releases in 3 days
entries.author: Victor Kildahl (@VictorKildahl)
entries.blurb: Victor Kildahl answered the top reply to Arc's sunset post, 'open-source it', by building Cra, an open-source Arc for Mac. Three days in: 2,308 visitors, 500+ downloads, 62 GitHub stars, 16 releases.

entries.title: A crowd-sourced comparison sheet of Arc-like browsers, open for corrections
entries.author: Sridhar Katakam (@srikat)
entries.blurb: Sridhar Katakam is maintaining a Google Sheet comparing Arc-like browsers feature by feature and asking people who have tested them to flag missing or wrong cells, a sign of how many Arc successors appeared within a week of the sunset.

entries.title: Duck.ai adds end-to-end encrypted chat sync across devices and browsers with no account, email, or password
entries.author: DuckDuckGo (@DuckDuckGo)
entries.blurb: DuckDuckGo shipped chat sync for Duck.ai: conversations follow the user across devices and browsers, end-to-end encrypted so only the user can read them, with no account, email, or password required. Enabled from Settings, Chats, Sync and Backup.

entries.title: Enact exits stealth with a $30M pre-seed, Switzerland's largest, to give robots touch through their motors instead of sensors
entries.author: Lukas Ziegler (@lukas_m_ziegler)
entries.blurb: Zurich-based Enact raised a $30M pre-seed from redalpine, Notion Capital, and firstminute, with angels including Arthur Mensch and Yann LeCun, to measure force inside robot motors rather than with fragile external touch sensors. Founder previously built software for 1X's NEO.

entries.title: Amazon rewrites its SDE role guideline for the AI era: judge outcomes, not tool use, but 'if you haven't already, learn and apply AI as soon as possible'
entries.author: Terk Terkowitz, VP/Distinguished Engineer, Amazon
entries.blurb: Amazon published the memo behind its revised SDE role guideline: keep the role defined by customer and business impact, not by AI usage, since any AI-practice definition would be stale within a year. It still tells engineers to adopt AI now, calls token and LOC metrics flawed but correlated, and warns that teams not adopting are falling behind.

entries.title: Granola adds free unlimited voice typing in any app, joining the dictation pile-on
entries.author: Chris Pedregal (@cjpedregal)
entries.blurb: Granola, the meeting-notes app, shipped voice typing: unlimited words, free, working in any app, pitched as 'smol ship' by CEO Chris Pedregal. Another voice-first entry in a week that already saw Block's Dessa.
entries.take: you too, granola?

entries.title: Ollama's two-week model roundup: Muse-spark-open, Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash in cloud; Bonsai-2, Nemotron 3.5 local; a dozen 'decision models'
entries.author: ollama (@ollama)
entries.blurb: Ollama listed two weeks of additions: Beam, Muse-spark-open, MiniMax M3.1 Flash, Mistral Large 4, DeepSeek V4.1 Flash, and Clef in its cloud; Bonsai-2, EmbeddingGemma-2, Flint, Nemotron 3.5, and the Phonon TTS model locally; plus eleven 'decision models' including D1, Kev, and Pplx-decider.
entries.take: for those who trust and don't verify

entries.title: DuckDuckGo goes after Flock Safety's CEO over surveillance-camera scandals, police misuse, and security problems
entries.author: DuckDuckGo (@DuckDuckGo)
entries.blurb: DuckDuckGo's account says it watched Flock Safety CEO Garrett Langley's recent media appearances and took notes, as the license-plate camera company faces scandals over police misuse and cybersecurity problems. Third public swing at a bigger company by DDG this month.
entries.take: ballsy of them. i respect this

entries.title: Google admits AI search makes less money and will fix it with more ads; DuckDuckGo: 'Most innovative company on the planet.'
entries.author: DuckDuckGo (@DuckDuckGo)
entries.blurb: Quoting an Ars Technica report that Google admits AI search earns less than classic search and plans to close the gap with more ads, DuckDuckGo replied 'Most innovative company on the planet.' The post passed 41K views in hours.
entries.take: these guys, man..

entries.title: Sam Altman: local inference is 'a terrible allocation of scarce resources'; the world's limited DRAM should sit in the cloud at max utilization, not in laptops used 5% of the time
entries.author: morgan (@morqon)
entries.blurb: On the Cheeky Pint podcast, Sam Altman argued people wrongly assume open models solve inference locally, and that from a global allocation view it is 'quite terrible' to have the world's limited DRAM in personal computers used 5% of the time rather than at maximum utilization in the cloud.
entries.take: LOL

entries.title: Subvocal (YC F26): glasses that read tiny facial movements so you can talk to your AI without making a sound; $1.3M from YC and Afore
entries.author: David Lieb (@dflieb)
entries.blurb: David Lieb calls Subvocal's demo the most insane he has seen: glasses that track minute facial movements so the wearer can speak to an AI silently, built in four months by a YC F26 team that raised $1.3M from YC and Afore Capital so 'you never have to type or speak again'.
entries.take: voice prompting without the ... voice

entries.title: Wabi raises $55M Series A at $1.25B for 'personal multiplayer AI', an operating system for your life and the people in it
entries.author: Joonas Virtanen (@joonasvirtanen)
entries.blurb: Eugenia Kuyda's Wabi raised $55M at a $1.25B valuation led by IVP with a16z, Forerunner, Benioff, Tobi Lütke, and Marissa Mayer. Pitch: a personal AI that pulls your people, context, and apps together to coordinate plans and share the mental load, 'multiplayer' meaning shared across a household or group.
entries.take: wtf is "multiplayer AI"?

entries.title: Claude Code spends 16 to 20% of tokens re-sending each background agent's transcript every 30 seconds for a 3-word status line; a 70-line Bun preload turns it off
entries.author: Flamerix AI (GitHub Gist)
entries.blurb: Flamerix found via OpenTelemetry that Claude Code's agent_summary side-query, on by default since August, cost more than the main conversation (16.4% of spend, 1 in 5 requests, 96% on Opus). No setting disables it, so they shipped an MIT Bun preload that suppresses the timer without touching the binary. 120 stars.
entries.take: incredible use of free will to fight token waste

entries.title: Quinn Nelson: Safari on Mac has gotten so bad he can't use it; now on Helium, which is 'fine' but fast and never fails to load
entries.author: Quinn Nelson (@SnazzyLabs)
entries.blurb: Tech YouTuber Quinn Nelson says Safari on the Mac has too many bugs and slowdowns to keep using, partly because nobody targets it, and that he has switched to Helium, a Chromium-based browser he finds merely fine but fast and reliable. 52K views.
entries.take: Helium?!

entries.title: Browser Use open-sources browser-harness: let Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor drive your real logged-in Chrome; 'by far the most efficient browser harness for agents'
entries.author: Gregor Zunic (@gregpr07)
entries.blurb: Browser Use published browser-harness on GitHub, a CLI that lets Claude Code, Codex, or Cursor use the developer's real Chrome with existing logins, with co-founder Gregor Zunic calling it by far the most efficient browser harness for agents.

entries.title: 'You only need 2 things. Everything is either a CLI or a URL.'
entries.author: Andrew Qu (@andrewqu)
entries.blurb: Riffing on a 'you only need three things' meme, Vercel's Andrew Qu reduces the agent-era stack to two surfaces: everything is either a CLI or a URL. 21K views, in the same week Christina argued dashboards are not going anywhere.
entries.take: URL or CLI

entries.title: Brendan Eich: saw a Brave-on-Blink-on-iOS demo; 'can't say more, no promises' given tech risk and Apple as gatekeeper
entries.author: Brendan Eich (@BrendanEich)
entries.blurb: Quoting Open Web Advocacy's case that Apple's WebKit claims do not stand up and regulators should force browser-engine competition on iOS, Brave CEO Brendan Eich says he recently saw a demo of Brave running on Blink on iOS, with no promises given technical risk and Apple as gatekeeper.
